groups.title: Containment
groups.blurb: What a shell command may touch, and whether a run works in place or in a copy.

rows.label: Sandbox shell commands
rows.summary: Runs shell commands inside the operating system's sandbox, with writes limited to the project, temporary folders and package caches.

rows.label: Sandboxed commands may use the network
rows.summary: Lets sandboxed commands reach the network. Off, package installs and dev servers that fetch anything fail.

rows.label: Sandboxed commands may use Docker
rows.summary: Lets sandboxed commands reach Docker's or Podman's socket. A container can mount any folder on the machine, so this opens a way around the sandbox.

rows.label: Air-gapped mode
rows.summary: Only local models run. Web search is removed, the browser opens localhost only, and shell commands lose the network.

rows.label: Work in a copy after someone else's text
rows.summary: A run started from an issue, a pull request or a page works in a copy. Routine work in the copy runs; pushes, pull requests and MCP calls wait for one apply.

rows.label: Work in a copy when a task links to a site
rows.summary: A message that links to a site off this machine starts in a copy, before the page is read. Reading the page still marks the run as untrusted.

groups.title: Firewall
groups.blurb: What happens when a sandboxed command reaches a host.

rows.label: Network firewall
rows.summary: What the firewall does with hosts a sandboxed command reaches: off, observe every host, ask about unknown hosts, or allow only known ones.

groups.title: Approvals
groups.blurb: When a person is asked, and what the reviewer may approve.

rows.label: When to ask
rows.summary: Smart asks for risky calls and anything that leaves the project. Always ask asks for every side effect. Auto adds a reviewer that may approve calls that fit your policy.

rows.label: Review policy
rows.summary: The text the reviewer uses in Auto, and the policy that can make Smart ask. Up to 10,000 characters.

groups.title: Verification
groups.blurb: What a Build or Debug run has to show before it can call itself done.

rows.label: Verify before done
rows.summary: What a Build or Debug run that changed files must show: off, report failing checks, or block the done claim until they pass.

rows.label: Retries after a failed check
rows.summary: In block mode, how many times a failed verification goes back to the model.

rows.label: Time for the fail-to-pass check
rows.summary: Seconds the check may take, both checkouts together. 30 to 3,600.

rows.label: Strict new tests
rows.summary: A new or changed test that passes without the change fails verification instead of only warning.

groups.title: Second opinion
groups.blurb: A model from another lab reads the claim after the local checks.

rows.label: Second opinion model
rows.summary: The model from another lab that reads the claim. Unset, or the run's own lab, means no second opinion.

rows.label: Second opinion on done
rows.summary: Another lab checks a run's done claim once verification proves it or its checks pass.

rows.label: Second opinion on review findings
rows.summary: Another lab labels each finding a structured review kept.

groups.title: Models and spend
groups.blurb: The model new threads start on, the helper models, context and the daily cap.

rows.label: Daily spend cap
rows.summary: Runs pause and ask when today's spend reaches this amount. 0 turns the cap off. Counted per UTC day.

rows.label: Prices for other models
rows.summary: USD per million tokens for models Quaka has no built-in price for, as JSON, so the daily cap can count them.

rows.label: Reasoning effort
rows.summary: The default depth of thinking: the model's own, low, medium, high, extra high or max. Clamped to what each model accepts.

rows.label: Small model for side jobs
rows.summary: The provider and model for summaries, explore subtasks, review checks and automation conditions. Unset uses the thread's model.

rows.label: Model that describes images
rows.summary: Describes an image for a model that cannot see it. Unset uses the small model, then Claude Haiku when an Anthropic key is saved.

rows.label: Default model
rows.summary: The model new threads start with. The model menu writes it; runs Quaka starts on its own also read it.

rows.label: Decision layer
rows.summary: Asks a local model about real decisions in the background and logs its answers. It never decides anything.

rows.label: Half-price thread summaries
rows.summary: How a summary that a long thread needs is bought: off, flex, or flex and batch. A summary not ready when you send is cancelled and made at the normal price.

rows.label: Use each model's whole context window
rows.summary: Sends up to each model's whole context window instead of capping a thread at 200K tokens. Long threads cost more per message.

rows.label: Learned context windows
rows.summary: Context sizes learned from providers' too-long errors, for endpoints that do not publish them. Written by the app.

groups.title: Tools
groups.blurb: MCP, the browser, subagents, instructions and attachments.

rows.label: Load MCP tools on demand
rows.summary: With eight or more MCP tools connected, send a one-line index and load the schemas a step needs instead of every schema on every step.

rows.label: Let the agent script MCP tools
rows.summary: Offers a short JavaScript program over MCP results. Each MCP call the program makes still asks, as a direct call would.

rows.label: Parallel explore subtasks
rows.summary: How many read-only explore subtasks one turn runs at once. 1 to 16.

rows.label: Parallel writers
rows.summary: How many writer subagents run at once, each in its own worktree. 1 to 8.

rows.label: Also use the personal Claude Code instructions
rows.summary: Adds the personal Claude Code instructions file to every run. Off by default: another tool's personal file is not read without asking.

rows.label: Also use the personal Codex instructions
rows.summary: Adds the personal Codex instructions file to every run, or its override file when one exists. Off by default.

rows.label: Use your own browser
rows.summary: Lets the agent use your browser through Quaka's extension, with your signed-in sessions.

rows.label: Read-only MCP servers
rows.summary: Servers whose tools an undoable run may call directly, because they only read. Names are comma separated.

rows.label: Upload attachments once
rows.summary: Uploads attached images and PDFs to the provider once and references them by ID afterwards, instead of sending their bytes every step.

groups.title: Claude Code, Codex and ACP agents
groups.blurb: Agents that run their own loop, and how Quaka contains them.

rows.label: Sandbox Claude Code
rows.summary: Runs Claude Code's own process inside the sandbox and under the firewall, and routes its tool calls through Quaka's approvals.

rows.label: Sandbox Codex
rows.summary: Runs Codex's own process inside the sandbox and under the firewall.

rows.label: ACP agents
rows.summary: Agent Client Protocol agents Quaka can spawn and drive as the brain, with their launch commands.

rows.label: Custom providers
rows.summary: OpenAI-compatible providers added in Settings. Their keys stay in the operating system's keychain.

rows.label: Switch accounts when one runs out
rows.summary: When one Claude Code or Codex subscription account runs out mid-work, continue on the next saved account.

groups.title: Memory and sync
groups.blurb: Notes every thread gets, and the relay that carries threads between your devices.

rows.label: Use memory
rows.summary: Gives every thread the notes in Memory, with any model, including Claude Code and Codex.

rows.label: Sync relay
rows.summary: The relay device sync uses. Set per device when sync is turned on.

groups.title: GitHub
groups.blurb: Pull request watching, CI fixes and @quaka commands.

rows.label: Watch pull requests
rows.summary: Watches your pull requests for failing checks and review comments and starts a thread when one needs you.

rows.label: CI fix attempts
rows.summary: How many times Quaka tries to fix a failing check before it asks instead. 0 turns CI fixes off.

rows.label: Machine users
rows.summary: GitHub logins whose comments are ignored, separated by commas, spaces or newlines.

rows.label: @quaka commands
rows.summary: Per repository, whether @quaka comments can start or steer a thread, and whether issue comments count.

rows.label: Undoable fixes and replies
rows.summary: Runs CI fixes and review replies in a copy, with pushes and replies held for one apply.

rows.label: Dictation model
rows.summary: The speech-to-text model dictation uses.

rows.label: Banners
rows.summary: Banners for threads you cannot see: all, only what needs you, or off.

rows.label: Speak status
rows.summary: Speaks a thread's status through the operating system's speech engine.

rows.label: When to speak
rows.summary: Only while no Quaka window has focus, or always.

rows.label: Voice
rows.summary: A voice name from the system's available voices. Empty uses the system default.

rows.label: Speech volume
rows.summary: Speech volume, in percent. 10 to 100.

groups.title: Replay
groups.blurb: How many attempts a Replay task gets, and how long one may take.

rows.label: Repeats per task
rows.summary: How many graded attempts each task and config is topped up to. 1 to 20.

rows.label: Minutes per attempt
rows.summary: How long one Replay attempt may run before it is stopped and graded as it is. 5 to 240.

groups.title: Integrations
groups.blurb: The address the hosted team bot is managed through.

rows.label: Team bot address
rows.summary: The address the hosted team bot is managed through. Empty uses the default.
